_exposure_notes: Exposure time per frame. Multiplies the photon-rate spectra of A and B and the dark-current rate.

output._notes: npy (default): {run_id}_data.npy and {run_id}_expected.npy of shape (n_observations, ny, nx) in photoelectrons, plus {run_id}_truth.npz. fits: one file with DATA, EXPECTED and TRUTH. directory is relative to this config file (here: <repo>/simulated_data/sim_run_0001).

observations._notes: Each observation draws the listed parameters independently, models the expected image, then draws one noisy frame. Keys are aliases (x/y_position_arcsec, separation_arcsec, position_angle_deg, exposure_time_s, zernike_coefficients_m) or zodiax paths. normal: mean (default = configured value) and std; uniform: low, high. Values may be per-element lists.

optics._notes: radial_orders [2, 3] gives 3 + 4 = 7 Zernikes (defocus, astigmatism x2, coma x2, trefoil x2), so coefficients_m has 7 entries; observations.parameters.zernike_coefficients_m draws around them.

source._notes: Positions and separation in arcsec. position_angle_deg is the direction of B relative to A. (x, y) is a reference point a fraction centre_weight of the way from A to B: 0 = A, 0.5 = midpoint, F_B/(F_A+F_B) ~ 0.24 = photocentre, which nearly decorrelates the position from the separation (validation/reference_point_fisher.py).

spectra._notes: Photon-rate spectra: SED [photons/s/m^2/nm] x collecting area -> incident photons/s per bin; throughput is kept separate as filt_weights. n_coarse ~ 2K (K = constrainable spectral modes) propagates only n_coarse wavelengths and Hermite-interpolates the rest; null propagates all n_wavels. Here n_coarse = 2K per star with K = 16 (A), 13 (B) from validation/constrainable_modes.py for 10 co-fit frames; recompute if the spectra, throughput or frame count change.

throughput._notes: System throughput = product of components. The simulated band is where it exceeds threshold x peak (or band_nm if given); ~2.5% of detected photons fall outside 512-647 nm and are not simulated yet.

components._notes: Two sheets of glass at 0.91 each (visual estimate, as in photon_count.md)

detector._notes: Deterministic detector effects, applied inside telescope.model(). Layers on the oversampled grid (jitter, pixel geometry) come first, then the downsample to pixels, then per-pixel layers, in the order listed.

layers.name: pixel_response
layers._notes: pixel_response_map_path: .npy map; if null, a random flat 1 + flat_sigma * N(0, 1) is drawn from the seed.

noise._notes: Applied to the expected photoelectrons: Poisson, then Gaussian read noise.

miscellaneous_effects._notes: Not implemented yet: enabling any of these raises NotImplementedError.
